posts.title: Mushroom Clubs: What They Are and Why They’re Worth Joining

posts.title: Carbon Balls: Identification, Lookalikes, and Uses
posts.description: Carbon ball fungi (Daldinia childiae) look like a lump of charcoal or little black purses attached to a log. Carbon balls look nothing like a traditional mushroom and is easy to miss because it is so small and dark. The round, dark fungal balls grow on decaying hardwood, and their tough fruiting bodies can last through winters.

posts.title: Medicine from Fungi: Antibiotics, Cholesterol Pills, and Organ Transplant Drugs
posts.description: Fungi have been studied for medicinal properties for over a century, with some very important finds that have literally changed history. The best-known is penicillin, which arguably changed the course of WWII. Some fungi are used in medicine for organ transplants, as statins for high cholesterol, and to treat multiple sclerosis.
